siteTagline: Shared codebase meaning for people and coding agents
homeTitle: Ontology Atlas: codebase ontology for coding agents (MCP)
keywords: ontology, codebase ontology, code knowledge graph, MCP server, Claude Code, Codex, coding agents, software architecture

descriptions.home: Keep understanding your system as coding agents change its code. Share context, inspect recorded meaning and evidence, and keep it in a local Markdown folder.
descriptions.download: Download Ontology Atlas to share codebase context with agents and inspect meaning, evidence and unknowns. Signed macOS app, Windows beta, no Atlas backend.
descriptions.topology: See your project's domains, capabilities, elements and dependencies as one map. Each file's info block is the map, and the files stay on your own disk.
descriptions.docs: Read and edit the markdown folder directly. Change the info block at the top of a file and the map follows.
descriptions.projects: Every project and hub on this map, with the domains and capabilities each one is made of.
descriptions.guide: Start with a Markdown folder, connect your coding agent, and learn how to inspect recorded meaning, evidence, and unknowns in Ontology Atlas.
descriptions.changelog: Ontology Atlas release notes: what changed in the desktop app, the map, the MCP server and the CLI, release by release with dates, newest first.
descriptions.library: Gather sources, write wiki pages from them, and ask questions that cite their passages, all inside your local Markdown folder.
descriptions.agents: See the coding agents on this computer and connect them to Ontology Atlas over MCP.
descriptions.automations: Schedule ontology reviews and document checks that run on your computer and leave proposals for you to review.
descriptions.git: Review your folder's Git history, read each change as a document, and restore a single file.

projectTitles.ontologyAtlas: How Ontology Atlas is built: its own ontology

projectDescriptions.ontologyAtlas: Ontology Atlas described by its own ontology: the domains it is made of, the capabilities each one owns, and how they depend on each other.

guideDescriptions.whatIsAnOntology: What an ontology is: concepts, kinds, relations and agreed meaning, how it differs from a taxonomy, schema or knowledge graph, and one for a codebase.
guideDescriptions.atlasCompared: How Ontology Atlas compares with code graphs, repository wikis, Obsidian and Notion, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, and graph databases, and when to use each.
guideDescriptions.firstFiveMinutes: Getting started with Ontology Atlas: download the app or try the browser, open or create an ontology folder, and connect Claude Code or Codex.
guideDescriptions.readingTheMap: Reading the Ontology Atlas map: domains, capabilities and elements, relation lines, the concept panel, and stale or unknown code evidence.
guideDescriptions.vaultStructure: The Atlas ontology folder: one Markdown file per concept, the fields in the info block at its top (uid, slug, kind, title, display names, relations) and layout.
guideDescriptions.whatBecomesANode: How to choose concepts for a codebase ontology: when something is a domain, capability, element or document, and the one-sentence test.
guideDescriptions.relations: Typed relations in an Atlas ontology: depends on, related, broader, containment; how to write them in a file's info block and query them with MCP and the CLI.
guideDescriptions.studio: Editing an Atlas ontology: change relations and concepts on the map, review agent-proposed edits from Claude Code or Codex, and handle file conflicts.
guideDescriptions.fromYourRepo: Build a first codebase ontology from your repository: a coding agent reads the code over MCP, proposes concepts and relations, and you approve before saving.
guideDescriptions.connectAgent: Connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Antigravity to your codebase ontology over MCP, check the connection, and see what the agent can read and write.
guideDescriptions.growingVault: Keep your codebase ontology current as code changes: sync after edits, rename with backlinks, catch stale evidence, avoid duplicates, and commit with Git.
guideDescriptions.cli: The Ontology Atlas CLI: run it from source, look up and edit concepts, check health, and see how it shares one engine with the MCP server agents use.
guideDescriptions.trust: Data, privacy and safety in Ontology Atlas: what stays on your disk, what can leave it and when, MCP agents, and signed macOS and unsigned Windows builds.
